title: Read files and search a codebase
contract: `read_file` — line-numbered, paginated (`offset`/`limit`, 1-indexed), auto-extracts readable text from common document formats (PDF/docx/…), per-line cap `tool_output.max_line_length`, and is the one tool pinned to an infinite spill threshold so persist→read→persist cannot loop. `search_files` — ripgrep-backed content regex OR glob file-finding, explicitly the replacement for `grep`/`rg`/`find`/`ls` in the terminal, `max_result_size_chars=100_000`. Rolls up 2 entries.
governance: read-only, but the root scope IS the security boundary — search must honour the identical `JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS` / symlink / secret-name rules as file_read, not reimplement them
remaining_verbatim: Document extraction beyond .pdf and .docx is not built: no .xlsx, .pptx or other extractor exists, and DOC_EXTS and the parser table list only those two (agents/core/local_docs.py:28, agents/core/file_tools.py:201-202). The Hermes row names 'PDF/docx/…' and the gap stays open. Honest limits of what is built: (1) regex search is Python `re`, not ripgrep, so ripgrep's linear-time completion is not available: a catastrophic-backtracking pattern that CPython cannot finish, and that the static (a+)+ guard does not catch such as (a|aa)+$, stops at the 10 second deadline with stopped_by=deadline and returns only the rows of files whose search finished; regex semantics (\w \b \s, Unicode classes, no PCRE or POSIX features) are Python's, and flavour-dependent constructs are refused rather than translated. (2) With no Python interpreter to start (a frozen build) regex=true returns regex_unavailable; literal and glob search still work. (3) .gitignore handling is the cheap subset: only the searched root's own .gitignore is read, only plain directory names or paths (wildcard lines are ignored), and any '!' line disables it entirely; the fixed NOISE_DIRS list is still pruned. (4) One directory holding millions of entries is still listed in full by os.walk before the entry, file and deadline caps run, so the caps bound the walk between directories, not inside one. (5) Content search skips files larger than max_bytes (default 2,000,000) and binaries, matches a literal on only the first 8 KiB of each line, and returns bounded snippets with path and line (no context lines); the result is bounded by match counts (at most 500 rows, 20 per file), not by a configurable character budget like Hermes's max_result_size_chars. (6) Line numbers are opt-in (line_numbers=true), not the default of every read, and are not applied to byte pages or images.

original_dependency_note: nothing (skipped); the react_to_message carve-out depends only on channels/manager.py
historical_exclusion_reason: Skip for product reasons, not effort. Discord server administration (roles, pins, moderation) serves a community-manager user Nerva does not have; Feishu/Lark and Yuanbao serve a China enterprise market Nerva does not target and cannot support. More importantly these tools encode a shape Nerva has deliberately rejected — an agent acting inside someone else's platform with that platform's admin credentials — whereas Nerva's channel model is the owner's own house talking to the owner. `social.py` already shows the right pattern: every outbound write behind approval, credentials resolved at action time and never held by the model. Re-open path: if a household or small-company customer asks for Discord specifically, port `discord` (read + thread) only — never `discord_admin`. One entry here IS worth copying cheaply: `react_to_message`, because acknowledging with an emoji instead of a paragraph is real conversational manners on Telegram/WhatsApp/Signal, and Nerva's channels have no equivalent.
